issues.description: Method SealSaloon.orderMeal: the problem statement UML declares orderMeal(Meal): void (problem_statement.md line 31), but the solution implements public boolean orderMeal(Meal) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 12). This mismatch in the declared return type (void vs boolean) creates confusion about the expected contract and may cause tests or grading code that expect a void method to fail or students to implement the wrong signature. The template Main also calls shop.orderMeal(...) (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 16) without using a return value, which is consistent with a void signature and highlights the inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution implementation to match the problem statement by declaring public void orderMeal(Meal meal) and remove its boolean return values, or (B) update the problem statement UML and any tests/templates to specify orderMeal(Meal): boolean if a status return is intended. Ensure Main and any tests are updated accordingly so all artifacts agree on the same return type.
